strongest_angle: Researchers at the University of Tübingen discovered that carrion crows make visual decisions in an average of 235 milliseconds, processing moving dots twice as fast as humans and primates.

key_facts.fact: Researchers Philipp Schmidbauer and Andreas Nieder at the University of Tübingen tested decision speed in carrion crows and published their findings in Science.
Two carrion crows required an average of only 235 milliseconds to recognize the direction of a moving dot pattern on a screen during experiments at the University of Tübingen.
Crows solved visual decision tasks roughly twice as fast as humans and monkeys while using the same mathematical logic despite different brain structures.
In a study published on October 22 in the journal Science, two carrion crows distinguished the direction of moving dots in an average of 235 milliseconds.
